title: the update's rollback finishes whatever signal arrives

findings.claim: a second Ctrl-C during the update's rollback escaped it (Exception caught only) and SIGTERM and SIGHUP had no handler on the update path: no ROLLBACK FAILED line, no update.rolled_back event, a half restored box (external review ESC-4)
findings.fix: tools/trialbox/update.py Stops: INT, TERM and HUP alike, raised once at a stoppable step, every later signal and every signal during a rollback said and ignored; the rollback catches BaseException; the error line and the audit event say the release; tests/unit/test_update_signals_h114.py

findings.claim: tools/apply_update.sh: a signal to the shell before the update path only removed the stage folder and the script went on to the next commands, the update path included
findings.fix: the shell ends on INT, TERM or HUP before the update path (130, 143, 129, nothing was changed) and leaves one during it to the update path; tests/unit/test_update_signals_h114.py test_s1, test_s2

findings.claim: streamed_payloads dropped in silence a signed payload that was no longer a file on the second read of the stick (external review 1409-2)
findings.fix: refused as UpdateFailed; tests/unit/test_update_signals_h114.py test_1409_2; the rehearsal's swapped-stream step (tools/rehearse_box/h95_probe.py)

findings.claim: the host restore took only restore.lock, so the nightly backup could run over the folders it was restoring (external review 1421-3)
findings.fix: the restore holds deploy/site/backup.lock for its whole run; tests/unit/test_update_signals_h114.py test_1421_3

findings.claim: an update run on the console's time limit (procgroup) gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 10 s later: a rollback the SIGTERM starts is killed part way and the box is between releases until tools/apply_update.sh rollback is run (review 1461-3)
findings.from: card H-114, reproduced by the external review of #1461 (7124127048), 2026-11-24
findings.fix: card H-114b (the integrator's ruling 7124945074): procgroup.run takes an optional grace (default ten seconds, as before); ops.do_update_apply passes the update's own limit; tests/unit/test_update_grace_h114b.py. The put-back left by a killed updater holds the recovery (H114-08)

findings.claim: a signal inside the first host-tree switch on a copied install left the moved files out of the rollback record: the compose file a dangling link while the update said back on the release before (review 1461-1)
findings.fix: host_tree install/switch/sync fill the caller's record as each file moves; test_1461_1

findings.claim: apply_update.sh ospatch: a signal while the OS patch was applied said nothing was changed and exited 130/143/129 (review 1461-2)
findings.fix: the update path's mark is set before the OS patch tool runs; test_1461_2

findings.claim: a put-back command left running by a killed updater ran beside the put-back of tools/apply_update.sh rollback (review 1461-3)
findings.fix: run_cmd records each command's process group while it runs; recover refuses while one is alive; test_1461_3

findings.claim: an update started under nohup was rolled back when the session closed: Stops replaced the inherited ignore of SIGHUP (review 1461-4)
findings.fix: a signal the caller ignores stays ignored; test_1461_4

findings.claim: the nightly that meets a host restore says another backup run holds the lock, and the night has no backup without saying so (review 1461-5)
findings.fix: the reviewer's patch is for backup_schedule.py, which #1455 holds

findings.claim: a rollback cut short (SIGKILL) after a stop inside the host-tree switch left recover a point.json without the moved files: previous release said with the compose file still set aside (review 1461-1, the part left)
findings.fix: the rollback saves the rollback point before its put-back; test_1461_1_a_rollback_killed_after_a_stop_in_the_switch_is_finished_by_recover

findings.claim: a running-command record was trusted by its group id alone (an earlier boot's record, or the id now another's, held the recovery) and sat in a folder a bundle named running could own (review 1461-6)
findings.fix: the record names the boot and the leader's start time, in deploy/updates/.running; test_1461_6

findings.claim: the host-tree rollback lost a site's own link at a release path, and left aside a site file a new release path displaced on a box already on a host tree (review 1461-7)
findings.fix: sync sets a site's link aside as a file; restore after a switch puts back what was moved; test_1461_7

findings.claim: test_1461_1 sent its signal to the test run itself: a regression would end the whole run instead of failing one test (review 1461-8)
findings.fix: the case runs in a child process

findings.claim: a first signal while a command's running record was written left the command running and the rollback waiting for it (review 1461-9)
findings.fix: the record is written inside the try whose handler kills the group; test_1461_9

findings.claim: a SIGKILL inside the host-tree switch itself, before any rollback, left point.json with the record of before the switch: tools/apply_update.sh rollback said the previous release with the copied files still set aside (the half of review 1461-1 ruled to H-114c, High-class)
findings.fix: the switch saves the rollback point before each move; undoing a copied install's first host tree removes the links through current a cut-short switch never recorded; tests/unit/test_host_tree_switch_kill_h114c.py
findings.from: the integrator's ruling 7129325585 on the second review of #1461, 2026-11-24

findings.claim: in the grace after the limit's SIGTERM nobody read the group's pipes: a put-back that wrote more than a pipe holds blocked on its write and was SIGKILLed at the grace's end, part way (review 1472-1; update.run_cmd the same, ten seconds' grace)
findings.fix: procgroup._stop reads the pipes through the grace and ends it with the leader's exit or its time; procgroup.run and update.run_cmd use it; tests/unit/test_update_grace_output_h114d.py and the reviewer's test in test_update_grace_h114b.py
